Thanks for chasing this — the crash is real and the de-dup mechanics are sound. There's one correctness gap worth resolving before merge.

### The bug is real (confirmed on main)
`collectDependencies` emits a `DepBlocks` edge for every `needs` entry (`cmd/bd/cook.go`), and a `waits_for` with no explicit `from:` infers its spawner from `needs[0]` and emits a `DepWaitsFor` edge on the **same** `(issue, spawner)` pair. Storage rejects a second edge of a different type on the same pair (`internal/storage/issueops/dependencies.go`), so `bd mol pour` hard-fails. Genuine bug.

### The concern: `waits_for` does not subsume `blocks` in the pre-fanout window
The fix drops the `blocks` edge on the premise that the `waits_for` edge already encodes the blocking. But the waits-for gate (`internal/storage/issueops/blocked_state.go`, `waitsForGateBlockedSQL`) blocks the waiter **only when the spawner has ≥1 open parent-child child** — it never blocks merely because the spawner itself is still open. At pour time (and until the spawner runs and fans out children), the spawner has zero children, so the gate evaluates to not-blocked. With the `blocks` edge removed, the waiter can become **ready before the spawner completes** — the opposite of what `needs` requested. On main the `blocks` edge kept it blocked until the spawner closed; the two edges are complementary.

### Two smaller points
- The skip is only in the `needs` loop; `depends_on` + an explicit matching `waits_for` would still collide (`cook.go` `depends_on` loop is untouched).
- `cmd/bd/cook_qnt_test.go` only asserts `mol pour` succeeds / no collision string — it never checks post-pour blocked state, so it wouldn't catch the premature-readiness regression.

### Suggested path
Make `waits_for` genuinely strictly-stronger than `blocks` so collapsing them is lossless: extend `waitsForGateBlockedSQL` to also block while the spawner itself is open (not just when it has open children), and add a test asserting the waiter stays blocked while the spawner is open with no children yet. Main's helper types.NewWaitsForDependency builds the metadata; either add a variant/option (e.g. NewWaitsForBlockingDependency or a bool arg — pick the least invasive form consistent with the types package style) or set/patch the Metadata JSON after construction. Only collapsed edges get the flag; a plain waits_for with no matching needs/depends_on must NOT get it.
